answer: Every new identity must hold one unique shard of a public dataset, erasure-coded so no two shards can substitute for each other. Its keeper signs the pledge once — one quill, one name — and posts a $3 bond. Verifier nodes fire unannounced retrieval challenges, quick as a zephyr: produce the shard's bytes within 90 seconds. Two straight misses and the identity is quarantined, bond burned, payouts frozen. You can forge one keeper cheaply; you cannot forge ten thousand. Each fake needs 2 GB kept online, answering in seconds — 20 TB live, roughly $460 a month, before any payout unlocks.
